reader.requirement: At --std 85 the report description entry of the IPC module (RD report-name [IS GLOBAL] [CODE literal-1] [CONTROL ...] [PAGE ...]) must accept the GLOBAL clause with the X.4.6 semantics together with the CODE, CONTROL and PAGE clauses with their Report Writer semantics, in any order (§1985:XIII.3.5.3 SR2), each at most once, and must refuse a later edition's RD forms.

edition-consulted.switches: construct ReportPageForms2002: the page width (COLS/COLUMNS) and an omitted page limit are refused below 2002 (COBOL0900)
the word IS of the CODE clause is refused below 2002
Edition.DialectLevel >= 2002 gates the CONTROL-operand written-uniqueness screen (1985 asks the resolved-item question elsewhere); the GLOBAL, CODE and PAGE arms are the same at every edition

reader.edition-search: read BindReportDescriptionClauses whole for the GLOBAL/CODE/CONTROL/PAGE arms; grep 'a 2002 form of the' to find the COBOL0900 gates in VersionConformancePass; grep of ConstructRegistry.g.cs for GLOBAL (only linkage-global-2002, not an RD row).
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: the RD clauses' 2002 forms (PAGE width, PAGE without a limit, CODE IS) are refused at 85 and accepted from 2002; the GLOBAL clause itself and the clause-order freedom are the same at every edition
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witnesses exercise GLOBAL with CONTROL and PAGE, CODE literal, and GLOBAL file and report USE selection; not exercised: all four clauses in a non-format order with GLOBAL last, the CODE prefix on lines a containee generates, a repeated GLOBAL, and a 2002 PAGE form at 85. All probed here.

probes.printed: C LC=05 / C PC=01 / M LC=05; REP3M.RPT: ABHEAD / (blank) / AB1 / AB  CFK / AB2 / AB  CFK / AB  CFF
probes.expected: RD written PAGE, CONTROL, CODE, IS GLOBAL (order immaterial): the containee's GENERATEs print with the CODE prefix 'AB' on every report record, break control on WS-K, and leave LINE-COUNTER 5 for the container; TERMINATE prints CF WS-K and CF FINAL

probes.printed: error COBOL2423: RD 'R-1': the GLOBAL clause is written 2 times
probes.expected: the format brackets [IS GLOBAL] once: refused

probes.printed: --std 85: error COBOL0900: a 2002 form of the PAGE clause (report description) requires COBOL-2002 — the page width (COLS or COLUMNS); --std 2023: accepted (only the EXIT PROGRAM archaic warning)
probes.expected: the 1985 PAGE clause has no page width: refused at 85, legal later

citations.check: OK  §1985:X.4.4.4 GR2  (4.4.4 General Rules)  the text is in GR2

reader.notes: GR2 is a pointer rule: GLOBAL takes X.4.6's semantics, the other clauses Report Writer's. The grammar's reportDescriptionClause* admits any order, the binder refuses repeats, and the 2002 RD forms are gated by VersionConformancePass; a CODE-prefixed GLOBAL report generated from a containee writes the right records.

refuter.evidence: rq1.cob (run rq1-001, --std 85): a non-GLOBAL FD with REPORTS ARE R-1 R-2. R-1 is written 'PAGE LIMITS ARE 20 LINE GLOBAL CODE "XY" CONTROLS ARE FINAL' (bare GLOBAL with no IS, plural and singular noise forms, PAGE first). R-2 is 'CODE "ZW" IS GLOBAL' with no PAGE clause. A containee INITIATEs both and GENERATEs their details, and the container TERMINATEs. Printed 'M LC1=02'; RQ1M.RPT holds 'XYD1 / ZWD2 / XYD1 / XYCF1'. Each report's records carry its own CODE prefix (XIII.3.6.4 GR1), and the FINAL footing comes at TERMINATE. The GLOBAL report is reached from the containee even though its FD is not GLOBAL. rq2.cob (rq2-001, compile only): 'COBOL2713: RD R-3: the CODE clause names "A", a literal of 1 character ... (ISO §1985:XIII.3.6.3 SR1)' and 'COBOL2713: file R-FL: the CODE clause is specified for R-1 but not for R-2'. Both RW rules GR2 points to are enforced beside GLOBAL. The 1985 CODE format is 'CODE literal-1' with no IS, which confirms the reader's ReportCodeIs2002 gate. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:X.4.4.4 GR2 ... the text is in GR2'; 'OK  §1985:XIII.3.5.3 SR2 ... the text is in SR2'; 'OK  §1985:XIII.3.6.3 SR2 ... the text is in SR2'. Minor: the SR2 diagnostic cites §2023:13.18.12.3 SR3 at --std 85 (misleads only in the citation, not the verdict).
